sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Across centuries, artists and writers have tried to make sense of the mysterious force that brings ideas to life.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，艺术家和作家们一直试图理解赋予创意生命的神秘力量。

sentences.en: The ancient Greeks imagined the muse as a literal spirit, a whispering goddess who breathed inspiration into the poet's ear.
sentences.zh: 古希腊人将缪斯想象成一个真正的精灵，一个在诗人耳边低语、注入灵感的女神。

sentences.en: Renaissance painters courted her through ritual and prayer, while romantic poets look for her in storms, mountain peaks, and moonlit walks.
sentences.zh: 文艺复兴时期的画家通过仪式和祈祷来追求她，而浪漫主义诗人们则在风暴、山峰和月光下的漫步中寻找她。

sentences.en: Now, psychological research is discovering that what the ancients call divine inspiration is really the brain at play.
sentences.zh: 如今，心理学研究发现，古人所说的神圣灵感其实是大脑在进行的一场游戏。

sentences.en: When we are relaxed, taking a shower, folding laundry, staring out a window, our minds slip into a pattern of spontaneous association.
sentences.zh: 当我们放松下来，洗澡、叠衣服、凝视窗外时，我们的思维会进入一种自发联想的模式。

sentences.en: Neurons fire across disparate brain regions, linking old memories with half-formed ideas.
sentences.zh: 神经元在不同的脑区之间放电，将旧记忆与半成型的想法连接起来。

sentences.en: Then, suddenly, an insight bubbles up.
sentences.zh: 然后，突然之间，灵感涌现。

sentences.en: It feels like a gift from the heavens, but it's really the product of our own unconscious minds.
sentences.zh: 它感觉像是来自天堂的礼物，但它实际上是我们自己无意识大脑的产物。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, and in a companion story on Hidden Brain Plus, the origins of creativity, and how to find the muse within.
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，以及《隐藏的大脑·升级版》中的配套故事，将探讨创造力的起源，以及如何寻找内心的缪斯。

sentences.en: When we think about how creative work unfolds, we usually imagine it happening in moments of intense focus.
sentences.zh: 当我们思考创造性工作是如何展开的时候，我们通常会想象它发生在高度专注的时刻。

sentences.en: A painter standing before his canvas, a scientist peering into her microscope.
sentences.zh: 一个画家站在画布前，一个科学家凝视着显微镜。

sentences.en: But research shows that many of our most original ideas do not appear when we are concentrating hard.
sentences.zh: 但研究表明，我们许多最具原创性的想法并不是在我们高度集中注意力时出现的。

sentences.en: They arrive when our minds wander, when we're driving, showering, or staring into space.
sentences.zh: 它们出现在我们思维漫游的时候，当我们开车、洗澡或发呆的时候。

sentences.en: Op Dijkstra-Haus is a psychologist who recently retired from Ratboult University, Neumagen, in the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 阿普·迪克斯特拉-豪斯是一位心理学家，最近刚从荷兰奈梅亨的拉德堡德大学退休。

sentences.en: He studies the origins of inspiration and creativity.
sentences.zh: 他研究灵感和创造力的起源。

sentences.en: Op Dijkstra-Haus, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 阿普，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Op, you're familiar with the story of Friedrich August Kekule, a German chemist born in 1829.
sentences.zh: 阿普，你很熟悉弗里德里希·奥古斯特·凯库勒的故事吧，他是一位生于1829年的德国化学家。
zh_words: 弗里德里希·奥古斯特·凯库勒

sentences.en: What was the great research project of his life?
sentences.zh: 他一生中伟大的研究项目是什么？

sentences.en: Kekule was working on the structure of molecules that was in the 1860s, what the most famous chemists did.
sentences.zh: 凯库勒当时在研究分子的结构，那是在19世纪60年代，这是当时最著名的化学家们所做的事情。

sentences.en: And some of the structures were known by then.
sentences.zh: 到了那时，其中一些结构已经为人所知了。

sentences.en: We knew what water looked like or oxygen.
sentences.zh: 我们知道水或氧气是什么样子的。

sentences.en: But Kekule was working on more complex molecules.
sentences.zh: 但凯库勒当时在研究更复杂的分子。

sentences.en: So these complex molecules often were related to carbon and how carbon molecules took the form of long chains, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这些复杂的分子通常与碳有关，以及碳分子如何形成长链，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没、错。

sentences.en: And he was, I think, at the time working on what they called benzene, which is part of crude oil.
sentences.zh: 而且我想他当时正在研究他们所说的苯，它是原油的一部分。

sentences.en: And he was working on it for quite a while.
sentences.zh: 他研究了相当长一段时间。

sentences.en: He couldn't figure out the structure of that molecule.
sentences.zh: 他一直搞不清楚那个分子的结构。

sentences.en: And at some point, he thought about it, he thought about it, and he thought about it even more.
sentences.zh: 在某个时候，他一直在想，一直在想，想得更多。

sentences.en: And then he dozed off in front of his fireplace and he fell asleep.
sentences.zh: 然后他在壁炉前打了个盹，睡着了。

sentences.en: And in his dream, he suddenly saw a snake biting its own tail.
sentences.zh: 在梦中，他突然看到一条蛇在咬自己的尾巴。

sentences.en: And he woke up, startled, and he suddenly knew that benzene had the shape of a ring.
sentences.zh: 他惊醒过来，突然知道苯的形状是一个环。

sentences.en: So in other words, these carbon molecules had these long chains, but the insight that he got
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这些碳分子有长链，但他得到的洞察是，

sentences.en: while he was sleeping was that this long chain in some way circled back on itself and formed a ring.
sentences.zh: 当他在睡觉时，这个长链不知何故回环连接并形成了一个环。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: In a dream.
sentences.zh: 在梦中。

sentences.en: And that was, at the time, completely new.
sentences.zh: 在当时，这绝对是全新的。

sentences.en: Nobody had thought about it.
sentences.zh: 没有人想到过这一点。

sentences.en: He must have been very startled to have woken up from this dream with this dream of a snake and realized that in some ways it had solved this problem.
sentences.zh: 他从这个梦中醒来，带着这个蛇的梦，并意识到它在某种程度上解决了这个问题，他一定非常震惊。

sentences.en: He was shocked.
sentences.zh: 他很震惊。

sentences.en: Yeah, he was shocked himself.
sentences.zh: 是的，他自己也很震惊。

sentences.en: And of course, also elated because he immediately realized that it was not just a dream, that it was the solution.
sentences.zh: 当然，他也欣喜若狂，因为他立刻意识到这不仅仅是一个梦，这就是解决方案。

sentences.en: He must have been euphoric as well.
sentences.zh: 他当时一定也欣快若狂。

sentences.en: So some years after that discovery, a French scientist and mathematician, Henri Poincaré, was working on a problem related to what are known as fusion functions.
sentences.zh: 在那项发现几年后，一位法国科学家兼数学家亨利·庞加莱正在研究一个与所谓“自守函数”（编注：此处原文fusion functions为fuchsian functions的误听，译为富克斯函数或自守函数均可，此处保留常见学术直觉）相关的问题。

sentences.en: Again, like Kekulé, he found himself stumped?
sentences.zh: 和凯库勒一样，他也发现自己被难住了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Poincaré did all kinds of different things.
sentences.zh: 庞加莱做过各种各样不同的事情。

sentences.en: He was really almost a universal scientiSt. But one of the things he did was indeed Fuchsian equations that he worked on,
sentences.zh: 他几乎算是一个全才科学家。但他做的事情之一确实是富克斯函数，他在上面下了功夫，

sentences.en: I think for seven or eight years already.
sentences.zh: 我想大概有七八年了。

sentences.en: And he made some progress, but there was a big puzzle that he couldn't solve.
sentences.zh: 他取得了一些进展，但有一个大难题他无法解决。

sentences.en: Then at a day where he wasn't going to work, he was in the countryside doing something completely different.
sentences.zh: 然后有一天，他本不用去上班，他在乡村里做着完全不同的事情。

sentences.en: And he stepped on a bus.
sentences.zh: 他踏上了一辆公交车。

sentences.en: And the moment he stepped on the bus, almost the exact millisecond, he saw the solution.
sentences.zh: 就在他踏上车的那一刻，几乎就在千分之一秒，他看到了解决方案。

sentences.en: He just knew it.
sentences.zh: 他就是知道了。

sentences.en: And it felt like it came out of nowhere.
sentences.zh: 感觉它凭空出现。

sentences.en: But he knew the solution.
sentences.zh: 但他就是知道了答案。

sentences.en: One of the striking things was, in both the Kekulé story, as well as in the Poincaré story, the answer seemed to come almost effortlessly.
sentences.zh: 最引人注目的一点是，无论是凯库勒的故事，还是庞加莱的故事，答案似乎都来得毫不费力。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: If you have one of those sudden flashes of insight or inspiration, it feels like it comes out of nowhere.
sentences.zh: 如果你有那种突然闪现的灵感或启发，感觉它就像是凭空冒出来的。

sentences.en: And for a long time, people believed these insights came from God.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，人们相信这些灵感来自上帝。

sentences.en: Or in the old Greek days, the time of the old Greek philosophers, they thought it came from Muses, the nine goddesses.
sentences.zh: 或者在古希腊时期，古希腊哲学家们的时代，他们认为它来自缪斯，那九位女神。

sentences.en: And Poincaré was probably the first one who explicitly said it, you know, it came from your brain, but it's in an area of your brain where you just can't reach.
sentences.zh: 而庞加莱可能是第一个明确说出来的人，你知道的，它来自你的大脑，但它位于你根本够不到的大脑区域。

sentences.en: And at a certain point, you have this sudden flash of insight.
sentences.zh: 然后在某个特定的时刻，你突然有了这种灵感的闪现。

sentences.en: Henri Poincaré wrote about his epiphany.
sentences.zh: 亨利·庞加莱写下了他的顿悟。

sentences.en: And it's, I think, instructive to listen to his words directly.
sentences.zh: 我想，直接听听他的原话会很有启发性。

sentences.en: He describes getting on this bus.
sentences.zh: 他描述了自己上这辆公交车的经历。

sentences.en: And he writes, we entered an omnibus to go someplace or other.
sentences.zh: 他写道，我们上了一辆公共汽车去某个地方。

sentences.en: At the moment when I put my foot on the step, the idea came to me without anything in my former thoughts seeming to have paved the way for it, that the transformations I
sentences.zh: 就在我把脚踏上台阶的那一刻，这个想法出现在我脑海中，此前我脑海中的任何想法似乎都没有为此铺平道路，我曾用以定义富克斯函数的变换，

sentences.en: had used to define the fusion functions were identical with those of Euclidean geometry.
sentences.zh: 与欧几里得几何的变换是完全相同的。

sentences.en: I did not verify the idea.
sentences.zh: 我没有去验证这个想法。

sentences.en: I should not have had time.
sentences.zh: 我也没有时间。

sentences.en: As upon taking my seat in the omnibus, I went on with a conversation already commenced, but I felt a perfect certainty.
sentences.zh: 正如我在公交车上落座后，继续着已经开始的谈话一样，但我感到了绝对的确定。

sentences.en: So this is another quality of these epiphanies,
sentences.zh: 所以这是这些顿悟的另一个特质，

sentences.en: Arp, which is that they not only come to us out of the blue, but when they come to us, we feel like we have absolute certainty that they must be right.
sentences.zh: 阿普，那就是它们不仅凭空降临，而且当它们降临的时候，我们会觉得有一种绝对的把握，它们一定是正确的。

sentences.en: Yeah, the sudden burst of inspirations are wonderful in different ways.
sentences.zh: 是的，突然迸发的灵感在各个方面都妙不可言。

sentences.en: One of them is indeed, if scientists have these ideas, they, yes, they feel absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 其中之一确实是，如果科学家们有了这些想法，是的，他们会觉得绝对正确。

sentences.en: And some people describe these moments of insight basically as love.
sentences.zh: 有些人基本上将这些灵光一现的时刻描述为爱。

sentences.en: They give you a lot of energy at the same time.
sentences.zh: 它们同时为你注入了大量的能量。

sentences.en: And the third thing is that it feels almost magical.
sentences.zh: 第三点是它感觉几乎带有某种神奇色彩。

sentences.en: And that's why you feel forced to do something with it.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你会觉得不得不对它采取点行动。

sentences.en: You can't have a wonderful moment of insight and then say, oh, but I'm going to ignore it for the forthcoming three days.
sentences.zh: 你不可能经历了一个美妙的灵感时刻，然后说，噢，但我接下来三天要忽略它。

sentences.en: I just, you know, I'm now going to do something completely different.
sentences.zh: 我只是，你知道的，现在要去干点别的完全不同的事。

sentences.en: That's impossible.
sentences.zh: 那是不可能的。

sentences.en: I understand that after this experience, Henri Poincaré changed the way he worked.
sentences.zh: 我了解到，经历过这次体验后，亨利·庞加莱改变了他的工作方式。

sentences.en: How so,
sentences.zh: 怎么个改变法，

sentences.en: Op?
sentences.zh: 阿普？

sentences.en: What did he do?
sentences.zh: 他做了什么？

sentences.en: Well, Poincaré said, okay, if my unconscious works on mathematical problems,
sentences.zh: 嗯，庞加莱说，好吧，如果我的无意识在处理数学问题，

sentences.en: I should give it time.
sentences.zh: 我应该给它时间。

sentences.en: So what he started to do is he worked only four hours a day, two in the morning and two in the afternoon, at least in a conscious way.
sentences.zh: 所以他开始的做法是，他一天只工作四个小时，早上两个小时，下午两个小时，至少在有意识的层面是这样。

sentences.en: He worked in a conscious way four hours a day.
sentences.zh: 他在有意识的层面上每天只工作四个小时。

sentences.en: And the rest of the day, he assumed that his unconscious would work on the problems he was working on.
sentences.zh: 而在一天中剩下的时间里，他假设他的无意识会继续处理他一直在研究的问题。你讲了一个非常精彩的故事，涉及科学家劳伦斯·布拉格。

sentences.en: You tell a wonderful story involving the scientist Lawrence Bragg.
sentences.zh: 你讲了一个非常精彩的故事，涉及科学家劳伦斯·布拉格。

sentences.en: Who was he up and how did he spend his time?
sentences.zh: 阿普，他是谁，他是怎么消磨时间的？

sentences.en: Lawrence Bragg was the youngest Nobel Prize winner ever.
sentences.zh: 劳伦斯·布拉格是有史以来最年轻的诺贝尔奖得主。

sentences.en: I think he still is.
sentences.zh: 我想他现在依然是。

sentences.en: He won, he was 25 or 26 when he won the Nobel Prize in physics.
sentences.zh: 他获奖时只有25岁或26岁，获得了物理学奖。

sentences.en: And what he did, he had one day a week where he chose to, to go gardening rather than, rather than working in his lab.
sentences.zh: 他所做的是，他每周有一天选择去园艺，而不是在实验室里工作。

sentences.en: And the assumption, of course, is that he was working on his, his, his scientific problems unconsciously.
sentences.zh: 当然，这背后的假设是他在无意识地研究他的科学问题。

sentences.en: And, and what is, uh, especially amusing about the story is that he was tending the garden of a, of an elderly lady in, in London,
sentences.zh: 而且，这个故事特别有趣的地方在于，他当时正在伦敦一位老太太的园子里帮忙打理花草，

sentences.en: uh, who didn't even know that she had this very famous gardener.
sentences.zh: 而这位老太太甚至不知道自己有这么一位大名鼎鼎的园丁。

sentences.en: So until, and it lasted until one of her friends came and, and she stood there in front of the window looking outside in the garden.
sentences.zh: 直到有一天，她的一个朋友来了，她站在窗前向外看着花园。

sentences.en: And she said, um, my dear, do you realize that the Nobel laureate, Sir Lawrence Bragg is actually pruning your hedges?
sentences.zh: 她说道，亲爱的，你意识到诺贝尔奖得主劳伦斯·布拉格爵士实际上正在修剪你的树篱吗？

sentences.en: And before that, she, she didn't have an idea that she, she probably had the most famous gardener.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，她完全不知道自己可能拥有最著名的园丁。

sentences.en: But yeah, he really believed in the importance of sometimes doing something completely different.
sentences.zh: 但确实，他非常坚信偶尔做一些完全不同的事情的重要性。

sentences.en: For centuries, we've been told stories about inspiration as something that visits us, a spark from the gods, a sudden gust of grace.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，关于灵感，我们听到的故事都是把它描绘成一种来访的体验，来自神明的火花，一阵突如其来的恩典。

sentences.en: Science is now finding that the spark is already burning inside us.
sentences.zh: 而科学现在发现，这火花已经在我们体内燃烧了。

sentences.en: And there are things we can do to give the spark oxygen.
sentences.zh: 我们可以做很多事情来给这火花提供氧气。

sentences.en: When we come back, how the brain comes up with original ideas.
sentences.zh: 休息过后，我们将探讨大脑是如何产生原创想法的。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: I remember reading a poem by Percy Bysshe Shelley many years ago.
sentences.zh: 我记得很多年前读过珀西·比希·雪莱的一首诗。

sentences.en: In Hymn to Intellectual Beauty, which is partly about the nature of inspiration, he writes,
sentences.zh: 在《理智颂》中，这首诗部分关于灵感的本质，他写道，

sentences.en: Sudden thy shadow fell on me.
sentences.zh: 突然你的阴影降临在我身上。

sentences.en: I shrieked and clasped my hands in ecstasy.
sentences.zh: 我狂喜地尖叫并紧紧双手交握。

sentences.en: This idea that inspiration comes out of nowhere, that it is unpredictable, untamable.
sentences.zh: 灵感凭空出现、不可预测且无法驯服的这种观念。

sentences.en: This is a very old idea.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常古老的观点。

sentences.en: Op Dijkstrahaus is a psychologist who studies the science of inspiration and creativity.
sentences.zh: 阿普·迪克斯特拉豪斯是一位研究灵感与创造力科学的心理学家。

sentences.en: Op, one of the most intriguing ideas in your work is that you have found that the brain has the
sentences.zh: 阿普，你研究中最吸引人的观点之一是，你发现大脑具有一种能力，

sentences.en: capacity to continue to work on problems even when our attention has turned to other things.
sentences.zh: 即使用户的注意力已经转向其他事情，它仍能继续处理问题。

sentences.en: How does this happen?
sentences.zh: 这究竟是如何发生的？

sentences.en: Most of us think that we focus on problems and then we solve those problems because we're focused on them.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人认为，我们专注于问题，然后因为我们专注于它们，所以我们解决了这些问题。

sentences.en: I once wrote a children's book about psychology and I compared thinking to a whale.
sentences.zh: 我曾经写过一本关于心理学的儿童读物，我把思考比作一头鲸鱼。

sentences.en: You know, a whale sometimes surfaces, but most of the time a whale is actually underwater and it still continues to swim.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，鲸鱼有时会浮出水面，但绝大多数时候鲸鱼其实都在水下，而且它还在继续游动。

sentences.en: And thinking is like that.
sentences.zh: 思考也是如此。

sentences.en: If we set ourselves important goals or if we work on something that we find very important, we think about it when we pay attention
sentences.zh: 如果我们为自己设定了重要的目标，或者如果我们正在研究我们认为非常重要的事情，我们在关注它时会思考它，但同样，在我们不关注它时，当我们正在做完全不同的事情时，比如看电影，我们的大脑仍在继续处理那个重要的问题。

sentences.en: what we did is we gave information about four different apartments in the city of Amsterdam.

sentences.zh: 第一组只是阅读信息并进行选择。

sentences.en: And the second group, they read the information.
sentences.zh: 而第二组，他们阅读了信息。

sentences.en: We told them to choose later on.
sentences.zh: 我们告诉他们稍后再做选择。

sentences.en: And first, they were distracted with a word puzzle, something simple.
sentences.zh: 首先，用一个字谜来分散他们的注意力，很简单的那种。

sentences.en: And then just a few minutes later, they were asked their favorite apartment.
sentences.zh: 就在几分钟后，他们被问及最喜欢的公寓是哪一套。

sentences.en: And they performed much better than the other group.
sentences.zh: 他们的表现比另一组好得多。

sentences.en: So if you give yourself a couple of minutes to unconsciously think about something, you make better decisions.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你给自己几分钟时间进行无意识的思考，你会做出更好的决定。

sentences.en: And we added a third group where we said to, after people read the information about the apartments, we said, well, you can forget about the information of the apartments.

sentences.en: And they failed again.

sentences.en: And in the second stage, other researchers showed that when people read the information about the apartments, certain brain areas become active.

sentences.en: They are, they're thinking about the apartments.

sentences.en: And then when you set a goal to later make a choice and you do these word puzzles, then the brain areas still continue to work on the apartments.
sentences.zh: 然后，当你设定了一个稍后做决定的目标并做了这些字谜时，大脑区域仍然会继续处理公寓相关的信息。

sentences.en: When you tell people you can forget about the information of the apartments, we're not going to use it.

sentences.en: The brain activity in that particular area stops.

sentences.en: So this is fascinating.
sentences.zh: 所以这太神奇了。

sentences.en: What you're finding is that when you tell people to focus on a problem to focus exclusively on the problem and come up with an answer, in some ways they do worse than
sentences.zh: 你发现的是，当人们被告知专注于一个问题，完全专注于这个问题并得出答案时，在某些方面，他们的表现反而不如

sentences.en: people who are asked first to focus on the problem and then do something else that's a little distracting and then return to the problem.

sentences.en: But the people who are told to focus on the problem and then forget about the problem, they in fact do not do as well as the people who are given the distraction task.

sentences.en: So in other words, focusing on something and being distracted for a little while is a great way to get your unconscious mind to continue to think about the problem.

sentences.en: But it's it's not it doesn't do so naturally.

sentences.zh: 是的，潜意识是不会为你代劳的。

sentences.en: Let's take a look at some of the qualities of unconscious thinking that can make it so generative.
sentences.zh: 让我们来看看无意识思考的一些特质，正是这些特质使其如此富有成效。

sentences.zh: 你说过，无意识的思维过程是广阔的，能够容纳比意识更多的信息。

sentences.en: Why would this be the case?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样呢？

sentences.en: It's simply a consequence of the of the enormous capacity of our brain and a rather limited capacity of consciousness.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是我们大脑巨大的容量与意识相对有限的容量所带来的结果。

sentences.en: Consciousness is one wonderful quality.
sentences.zh: 意识有一个极其美妙的特质。

sentences.en: It's very precise.
sentences.zh: 它非常精确。

sentences.en: You know, I could ask you, what's 14 times 17?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我可以问你，14乘以17等于多少？

sentences.en: And you can use a calculator.

sentences.en: But if you don't use a calculator, your consciousness can solve this within a few seconds.
sentences.zh: 但如果你不用计算器，你的意识也能在几秒钟内解出来。

sentences.en: The unconscious will never solve.

sentences.en: The amount of information you have to process in order to reach such a decision is really enormous.

sentences.en: And the unconscious mind has a, perhaps a wider aperture.

sentences.en: That's exactly what it is.

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly what it is.

sentences.en: And in a sense, also more creative.

sentences.en: And consciousness on the other hand, yeah, exactly.

sentences.en: is involved in, in sort of capturing the general feel of something, not necessarily the precise contours of, of many things.

sentences.zh: 潜在特征。我们做过一些实验，例如，人们必须对一个假想的人物形成一种印象。

sentences.en: And you describe this person with all kinds of behavioral information.
sentences.zh: 你用各种行为信息来描述这个人。

sentences.zh: 如果你随后询问人们对这个人的记忆，你会发现那些

sentences.zh: 有意识思考过这件事的人，对具体信息的记忆要好得多，例如读报纸这件事；

sentences.en: newspaper, for instance, and people who thought about it unconsciously, they have a feeling for what
sentences.zh: 而那些无意识思考过的人，他们对潜在特征有一种感觉——

sentences.en: the underlying trait is, is somebody forgetful or chaotic, or maybe very intelligent or, so you, you, the unconscious is more about the underlying meaning of things.
sentences.zh: 这个人是健忘、混乱，还是可能非常聪明？所以，潜意识更多关乎事物的潜在含义。

sentences.en: In the example we talked about earlier with Henri Poincaré, you know, he talks about how
sentences.zh: 在我们之前讨论亨利·庞加莱的例子时，你知道，他谈到了

sentences.en: the insight that he eventually had as he stepped onto this bus was an insight that allowed him to combine two ideas that in fact came from very different places.
sentences.zh: 当他踏上这辆公交车时最终获得的洞察力，这种洞察力让他能够将两个实际上来自截然不同领域的想法结合起来。

sentences.en: Um, talk about the idea that unconscious thought processes allow diverse ideas and experiences to mingle and combine in novel ways.
sentences.zh: 呃，谈谈这样一种观点：无意识的思维过程允许不同的想法和经验以新颖的方式交融和结合。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that, that is also one of the things unconscious thought is capable of doing,
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这也是无意识思维能够做到的事情之一，

sentences.en: you know, for instance, even childhood memories can, can be part of such an unconscious thought process.
sentences.zh: 你知道，比如，甚至童年记忆也可以成为这种无意识思维过程的一部分。

sentences.en: And it's almost like a definition of creativity that, that you combine things that aren't usually combined.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就是创造力的定义：把通常不会结合在一起的东西结合起来。

sentences.en: And this is something our, our unconscious is known to be better at than if we think about something very consciously, very attentively.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，与我们进行高度有意识、高度专注的思考相比，我们的潜意识在这方面更胜一筹。

sentences.en: And in some ways, this then connects with the idea that unconscious thought processes are going to be associative.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这就与无意识思维具有联想性的观点联系起来了。

sentences.en: In other words, one thing leads to the next and something from your childhood might intersect with something that happens in your workplace, which might intersect with something
sentences.zh: 换句话说，一件事引发另一件事，你童年的一幕可能会与你在职场中发生的事产生交集，进而可能与你在体育比赛中看到的事产生交集，

sentences.en: that you see in a sports game, whereas conscious thought processes are going to be more focused and convergent.
sentences.zh: 而有意识的思维过程则更具聚焦性和收敛性。

sentences.en: And so you can see how conscious thinking can lead us very systematically down a path, whereas unconscious thinking, you know, it can lead us into, you know, dead ends and blind
sentences.zh: 因此你可以看到，有意识的思考如何能非常系统地引导我们走上一条路径，而无意识的思考，你知道，它可能会把我们带入死胡同和盲

sentences.en: alleys, but it can also produce these unexpected connections that can lead to creativity.
sentences.zh: 区，但它也能产生这些能够通往创造力的意想不到的联系。

sentences.en: Yeah, first, it leads you deeper into the mire, as sometimes scientists say, but, but in the end,
sentences.zh: 是的，首先，它会把你带向更深的泥潭，正如科学家有时所说的那样，但最终，

sentences.en: yeah, it often leads you to, to the real solutions by using the most unusual associations and combinations.
sentences.zh: 是的，它往往会通过使用最不寻常的联想和组合，把你带向真正的解决方案。

sentences.en: One remarkable capacity of unconscious thought processes is that they seem to generate seemingly complete and perfect answers.
sentences.zh: 无意识思维过程的一个非凡能力在于，它们似乎能产生看似完整且完美的答案。

sentences.en: When Poincaré basically made his discovery, he said, you know,
sentences.zh: 当庞加莱基本上做出他的发现时，他说，你知道，

sentences.en: I felt a perfect certainty.
sentences.zh: 我感到了绝对的确定。

sentences.en: And he says later when he got home, for conscience's sake, I verified the result.
sentences.zh: 他后来还说，当他回到家后，为了良心起见，他验证了这个结果。

sentences.en: In other words, he said, I knew the result was correct already, but just to go through the motions, I had to, to verify it.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他说，我本来就知道结果是正确的，但为了走一下过场，我不得不去验证它。

sentences.en: Why would that be the case?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样呢？

sentences.en: Why would unconscious thought processes come up with more complete answers, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么无意识的思维过程能得出更完整的答案？

sentences.en: Well, we don't really know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们其实并不清楚。

sentences.en: And, and the unconscious doesn't do it all the time, unfortunately.
sentences.zh: 而且，遗憾的是，潜意识并不是每次都能做到这一点。

sentences.en: It only does so occasionally.
sentences.zh: 它只是偶尔为之。

sentences.en: But when your unconscious comes up with a solution to something, occasionally, it's just perfect.
sentences.zh: 但当你的潜意识偶尔为某事想出一个解决方案时，它简直是完美的。

sentences.en: There's no interference of, of consciousness.
sentences.zh: 没有任何意识的干扰。

sentences.en: It's just sort of truth arriving in its, in its purest form.
sentences.zh: 这就像某种以最纯粹形式降临的真理。

sentences.en: And you see it in many, many different areas, not just in science.
sentences.zh: 你可以在许多不同的领域看到这一点，不仅仅是在科学领域。

sentences.en: And if you look at popular music, what you see is that if you look at bands or musicians, the song that, that is written most rapidly is also the most famous.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看流行音乐，你会发现，如果你观察乐队或音乐家，那些写得最快的歌曲往往也是最著名的。

sentences.en: And with poetry, it's the same thing.
sentences.zh: 诗歌也是如此。

sentences.en: You know, some of the best poems were written in five or 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一些最好的诗是在五到十分钟内写出来的。

sentences.en: And Picasso, when he painted, he would immediately stop if he, if he felt that he was
sentences.zh: 毕加索在作画时，如果他觉得自己想得太多、开始有意识地思考了，他就会立刻停下来，

sentences.en: thinking about it too much, he was thinking consciously, he, it would just have to be, it would have to occur naturally to him.
sentences.zh: 这一切必须自然而然地发生。

sentences.en: And if it didn't occur naturally anymore, he would just stop.
sentences.zh: 如果不再自然流露，他就会直接停笔。

sentences.en: So yeah, there's something about the unconscious that it, that it can come up with something that is very pure, very beautiful.
sentences.zh: 所以，对，潜意识有这样一种特质，它，它能想出非常纯粹、非常美妙的东西。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, not every day, but it occasionally happens.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，并非每天如此，但偶尔会发生。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 你讲述了歌手兼词曲作家苏珊·维加的故事，她写了一首非常著名的歌，这首歌也是灵光一现浮现在她脑海里的。

sentences.en: What song was this?
sentences.zh: 这是什么歌？

sentences.en: Describe what happened to her up.

sentences.en: This, this is Luca.
sentences.zh: 这，这就是《卢卡》。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's her song, Luca.
sentences.zh: 这是她的歌，《卢卡》。

sentences.en: I remember watching a documentary about her on Dutch television and she showed her interviewer, the, the lyrics she wrote for Luca.
sentences.zh: 我记得在荷兰电视台看过一部关于她的纪录片，她向采访者展示了她为《卢卡》写的歌词。

sentences.en: And it was just a piece of paper that, that she showed.
sentences.zh: 那只是一张她展示给别人的纸。

sentences.en: And she said, this is when I, you know, the first time I wrote it and there were, nothing was crossed out.
sentences.zh: 她说，这就是我，你知道的，我第一次写下它的时候，上面没有任何涂改。

sentences.en: It was just there.
sentences.zh: 它就那样自然而然地诞生了。

sentences.en: She's, she, the lyrics just basically appeared to her and she only had to write them down.
sentences.zh: 她，她，歌词基本上就是自己浮现在她脑海里，她只需要把它们写下来就行。

sentences.en: And this is actually not too unusual.
sentences.zh: 这其实并不罕见。

sentences.en: A lot of musicians have one or two of such songs and they're usually their most famous.
sentences.zh: 很多音乐人都有过一两首这样的歌，而且通常也是他们最著名的作品。

sentences.en: Amy McDonald wrote, this is the life in about 15 minutes.
sentences.zh: 艾米·麦克唐纳写《这就是生活》只用了大约15分钟。

sentences.en: Now the song Luca is about child abuse.
sentences.zh: 现在这首歌《卢卡》是关于虐待儿童的。

sentences.en: It describes a story of a young boy who basically is, is being harmed, uh, presumably by his, uh, by his caretakers.
sentences.zh: 它描述了一个小男孩的故事，他基本上正在，正在受到伤害，嗯，据推测是由他的，嗯，由他的照顾者造成的。

sentences.en: Uh, and Suzanne Vega later said that in some ways the song was autobiographical, that she was writing about herself.
sentences.zh: 嗯，苏珊·维加后来表示，在某种程度上，这首歌带有自传性质，她写的是她自己。

sentences.en: And here again is an example of someone's musical abilities and talents intersecting
sentences.zh: 这里再次体现了一个人的音乐能力和才华与他们自己的童年经历交织在一起的例子

sentences.en: with their own childhood experiences and coming up with something that almost feels complete from the get go.
sentences.zh: 碰撞出了几乎从一开始就显得完美无缺的作品。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's a wonderful example of, of, yeah, an idea that is suddenly there and it's beautiful and it's pure and it's, yeah, it's finished.
sentences.zh: 这是一个绝佳的例子，关于，关于，对，一个突然涌现的想法，它是那么美妙、那么纯粹、并且，对，它是完整的。

sentences.en: You know, she didn't have to do much about it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她没怎么费心思去修改。

sentences.en: I think it was both the lyrics and the music were there within minutes.
sentences.zh: 我想歌词和音乐都是在几分钟内同时涌现的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's a wonderful, wonderful example of what you're, what a, what a creative unconscious can come up with.
sentences.zh: 这是一个绝妙无比的例子，展示了你，你的，你的创造性潜意识能迸发出怎样的成果。

sentences.en: My name is the second floor.
sentences.zh: 我的名字叫二楼。

sentences.en: I understand that, um, volunteers were presented once with riddles or problems that could be solved either through analysis or by sudden insight.
sentences.zh: 我了解到，嗯，曾向志愿者们出过一些谜题或问题，这些问题可以通过分析解决，也可以通过突然的顿悟来解决。

sentences.en: Uh, what kind of problems were these and, and what did, uh, what was the outcome of the experiment up?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些是什么类型的问题，还有，嗯，实验的结果是什么？

sentences.en: This is a tradition in cognitive psychology in the 1980s where people wanted to see, they wanted to study inside probleMs. And, uh, one example is, um, I think it goes like this.
sentences.zh: 这是20世纪80年代认知心理学的一个传统，当时人们想要看到，他们想要研究顿悟问题。并且，嗯，一个例子是，嗯，我想它是这样的。

sentences.en: So here's a riddle.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一个谜题。

sentences.en: Every day, water lilies double the surface area, uh, they occupy.
sentences.zh: 每天，睡莲覆盖的水面面积都会翻倍，嗯，它们所占的面积。

sentences.en: And at the start of the summer, there's only one lily leaf in the lake.
sentences.zh: 而在夏天开始时，湖里只有一片睡莲叶子。

sentences.en: After 60 days, the entire water surface is covered.
sentences.zh: 60天后，整个水面就被完全覆盖了。

sentences.en: On which day was the lake half covered with water lilies?
sentences.zh: 湖面被睡莲覆盖一半是在第几天？

sentences.en: Now, if you hear such a riddle, your conscious mind is inclined to just say, okay, so you start with one lily and then the next day there's two and then
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你听到这样一个谜题，你的意识倾向于直接说，好吧，你从一片睡莲开始，然后第二天是两片，然后

sentences.en: the third day there's four and then you, but this is not going to get you anywhere.
sentences.zh: 第三天是四片，然后你，但这根本毫无用处。

sentences.en: And what you need is insight.
sentences.zh: 你需要的是顿悟。

sentences.en: You, you need, uh, you need this sudden flash where you, you understand the riddle.
sentences.zh: 你，你需要，嗯，你需要那种灵光一现的瞬间，让你，你理解了这个谜题。

sentences.en: And this is usually, this usually occurs to you only when you take a little distance first and maybe even, you know, go and take a walk or something.
sentences.zh: 而这通常，这通常只有当你先拉开一点距离，甚至可能，你知道的，去散个步什么的，才会发生在你身上。

sentences.en: And then you realize, well, okay, if the, if after 60 days, the lake is fully covered and, uh, the number of leaves doubles every day, then of course,
sentences.zh: 然后你意识到，好吧，如果，如果在60天后，湖面被完全覆盖，嗯，叶子的数量每天翻倍，那么当然，

sentences.en: half covered means it's the day before the last day is on day 59.
sentences.zh: 覆盖一半意味着是在最后一天的前一天，也就是第59天。

sentences.en: And if the right answer comes to you, it comes in a sort of a flash.
sentences.zh: 如果正确的答案来到你身边，它会以一种灵光一现的方式出现。

sentences.en: It never, it never comes when you, when you approach it very analytically or consciously.
sentences.zh: 它绝不会，绝不会在你以非常分析或有意识的方式去对待它时出现。

sentences.en: One of the things I like about that puzzle is that in some ways it requires us to actually turn the problem on its head.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个谜题的原因之一是，在某种程度上，它要求我们把问题完全颠倒过来思考。

sentences.en: So in other words, instead of starting from day one and saying, okay, day one, there's one lily day two, there's two and so forth.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，不是从第一天开始说，好吧，第一天有一片睡莲，第二天有两片，诸如此类。

sentences.en: You actually start from the end and you say, okay, day 60, the lake is full and now working backwards.
sentences.zh: 而是实际从结尾开始，说，好吧，第60天湖满了，现在倒推回去。

sentences.en: When was the lake half full?
sentences.zh: 湖面什么时候是一半满的？

sentences.en: And in some ways it's, you're turning the problem on its head.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，你是在把问题颠倒过来。

sentences.en: And when you turn the problem on its head, the problem actually becomes easy.
sentences.zh: 当你把问题颠倒过来时，问题其实就变得简单了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And then understanding the problem by turning it on its head is already the solution because then you, once you know it, you know, it's, it's actually incredibly simple.
sentences.zh: 然后通过颠倒视角来理解问题本身就已经成了解决方案，因为一旦你知道了，你知道的，其实它极其简单。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Unconscious thought processes are operating even when we are asleep.
sentences.zh: 即使在我们睡觉时，潜意识的思维过程仍在运作。

sentences.en: Of course, uh, you write about a study in which volunteers who had experienced, uh, REM sleep were able to better solve problems requiring divergent thinking.
sentences.zh: 当然，嗯，你写过一项研究，其中经历过，嗯，快速眼动睡眠的志愿者能够更好地解决需要发散思维的问题。

sentences.en: Uh, tell me about this work.
sentences.zh: 嗯，跟我讲讲这项工作。

sentences.en: I think it started about 30 years ago where scientists discovered that during sleep, we engage in memory consolidation.
sentences.zh: 我想这始于大约30年前，当时科学家发现，在睡眠期间，我们会进行记忆巩固。

sentences.en: Uh, so this means actually if you learn something, then during REM sleep, we consolidate this information so that the next day we have better memory.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以这意味着实际上如果你学到了什么，那么在快速眼动睡眠期间，我们会巩固这些信息，以便第二天我们有更好的记忆。

sentences.en: And then people started to do more and more experiments and also more complex experiments
sentences.zh: 然后人们开始做越来越多的实验，还有更复杂的实验，

sentences.en: where in the evening participants in experiments would read quite complex information about the
sentences.zh: 在实验中，参与者在傍晚时分会阅读相当复杂的信息，内容关于

sentences.en: relationship of certain stimuli, like A is always bigger than B and B is always bigger than C and C is always bigger than D.
sentences.zh: 某些刺激之间的关系，比如A总是比B大，B总是比C大，C总是比D大。

sentences.en: But in later experiments, they made this information quite complex.
sentences.zh: 但在后来的实验中，他们把这些信息变得相当复杂。

sentences.en: And during the night people could sleep.
sentences.zh: 人们在夜间可以睡觉。

sentences.en: Other people did this during the day.
sentences.zh: 其他人则在白天进行这个实验。

sentences.en: So they, they also had eight hours until they came back to the testing room, but they couldn't sleep.
sentences.zh: 所以他们，他们也有八个小时的时间直到回到测试室，但他们不能睡觉。

sentences.en: And it turns out that during REM sleep, this is where people, uh, make these interesting connections and people,
sentences.zh: 事实证明，在快速眼动睡眠期间，正是人们，嗯，建立这些有趣的联系的时候，人们，

sentences.en: um, start to understand these very complex relations between stimuli.
sentences.zh: 嗯，开始理解刺激之间这些极其复杂的关系。

sentences.en: So only the group that slept during the night in a normal way could solve these, these, uh, these complicated probleMs. People who were woken up during their REM sleep couldn't.
sentences.zh: 因此，只有夜间正常睡觉的那组人才能解决这些，这些，这些复杂的难题。在快速眼动睡眠中被唤醒的人则不能。

sentences.en: And people who studied this during the day, uh, and so didn't sleep, uh, and so didn't sleep, they couldn't solve these problems either.
sentences.zh: 而那些在白天研究这个的人，嗯，因此没有睡觉，嗯，因此没有睡觉，他们也无法解决这些问题。

sentences.en: Now REM sleep has long been associated with dreaming.
sentences.zh: 现在，快速眼动睡眠长期以来一直与做梦联系在一起。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering in some ways if the process of dreaming is in fact a process of creativity because I, you know, unusual things get linked when we are dreaming.
sentences.zh: 我在想，在某种程度上，做梦的过程其实就是一个创造力的过程，因为我知道，当我们做梦时，不寻常的事物会被联系在一起。

sentences.en: Um, yes, indeed REM sleep is our, is basically our dream sleep.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，确实，快速眼动睡眠就是我们的，基本上就是我们的梦境睡眠。

sentences.en: And it's long been known that it is, it is indeed associated with creativity.
sentences.zh: 人们早就知道，它确实与创造力息息相关。

sentences.en: KQ Lay, of course, is a good example.
sentences.zh: 保罗·麦卡特尼（原文误作KQ Lay），当然就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: We know that yesterday, probably the most famous song by the Beatles, uh, the melody of yesterday was dreamt by Paul McCartney.

sentences.en: And, well, in the next 15 years, she had to work really hard to actually write all these seven novels.

sentences.en: But the idea came, yeah, during a train ride.

sentences.en: And it was, again, one of those examples of an idea that is both beautiful and pure and more or less finished at the same time.

sentences.en: It came to her and it was all there.

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 观看体育赛事，有非常多的事情在发生，它占用了你所有的心理空间。

sentences.en: But there are also experiences that we have that are quietly fascinating or softly fascinating where we are walking in nature.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些体验是安静吸引人或温和吸引人的，比如我们在大自然中散步。

sentences.en: So in other words, it's not like there's no stimulation coming in, but it's not hyper-stimulated.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，并不是没有刺激输入，但它不是过度刺激。

sentences.en: And riding a train is a little bit like that.
sentences.zh: 坐火车有点类似于此。

sentences.en: It's softly stimulating because things are changing.
sentences.zh: 它具有温和的刺激性，因为事物在变化。

sentences.en: The landscape is changing as the train is proceeding, but it's not changing so dramatically that it takes up all of your attention.
sentences.zh: 随着火车的行驶，风景在变，但它的变化并没有剧烈到占据你的全部注意力。

sentences.en: And it seems like it's in those situations that the mind is able to wander and come up with creative ideas.

sentences.en: Yeah, those moments are indeed the beSt. I studied the working habits of artists and scientists.
sentences.zh: 对，这些时刻确实是最好的。我研究过艺术家和科学家的工作习惯。

sentences.en: And what occurred to me is that most of them, especially work in the morning, some of them work
sentences.zh: 我注意到的是，他们大多数人，特别是在早晨工作，有些人工作的时间

sentences.en: more often than just in the morning, but the morning is usually the most productive time.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是在早晨，但早晨通常是最具成效的时间。

sentences.en: We know that people are, the cognitive abilities are usually at their best between about one and a half and five hours after you wake up.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，人们的认知能力通常在醒来后一个半小时到五个小时之间达到最佳状态。

sentences.en: Although that's not true for everybody, but it's true for most people.
sentences.zh: 尽管这并非对所有人都适用，但对大多数人来说确实如此。

sentences.en: And then in the afternoon, what you see is that many, many of them walk.
sentences.zh: 然后在下午，你会发现许多、许多人都在散步。

sentences.en: And walking is just one example of what you may call a lightly meditative state.
sentences.zh: 而散步只是你可能称之为轻度冥想状态的一个例子。

sentences.en: The same as the train ride, JK Rowling's train ride.
sentences.zh: 就像乘火车一样，J.K.罗琳乘火车的经历。

sentences.en: There's a few more of those.
sentences.zh: 还有更多这样的例子。

sentences.en: And yeah, those are indeed the most productive activities when it comes to unconscious thought.
sentences.zh: 对的，说到无意识思维，这些确实是最具成效的活动。

sentences.en: And I think there's two reasons.
sentences.zh: 我认为原因有两个。

sentences.en: One of them is that unconscious thought itself is working best under those conditions.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是，无意识思维本身在这些条件下运作得最好。

sentences.en: If you compare it with Times Square or to a situation where you are working very hard on something like a complex problem, your unconscious thought is not

sentences.en: And the second reason is that, of course, there has to be room.
sentences.zh: 第二个原因是，当然，必须要有空间。

sentences.zh: 意识中必须留出空间，好点子才能落地。

sentences.en: So if you're watching a very good movie, you're engrossed in the movie.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你正在看一部非常精彩的电影，你就会沉浸在电影中。

sentences.en: So you're not going to get any good ideas, at least not at that time.

sentences.en: And when you walk in nature, yeah, there's plenty of room in consciousness for, let's say, receive ideas from the unconscious, from your hidden brain.
sentences.zh: 而当你走进大自然时，是的，意识里有充足的空间，比方说，来接收来自无意识、来自你隐藏的大脑的想法。

sentences.en: So you say that a goal that engages the unconscious and generates insight should also be intrinsically oriented up.
sentences.zh: 所以你说，一个能够调动无意识并产生洞察力的目标，也应当具有内在的导向性。

sentences.en: What do you mean by this?

sentences.en: It's something you really like to do as opposed to extrinsic motivation.

sentences.en: A little bit of extrinsic motivation isn't necessarily bad, but if you want to last, if you want to persevere for a long time, you need intrinsic motivation.
sentences.zh: 一点点外在动机不一定是坏事，但如果你想持久，如果你想坚持很长时间，你就需要内在动机。

sentences.zh: 有一天，他醒来后，突然，他不再喜欢它了。

sentences.en: So in one of his more famous studies, if I remember this correctly, you know, he went up to people who were doing some
sentences.zh: 因此，在他的某项更为著名的研究中，如果我没记错的话，你知道的，他走到一些正在进行

sentences.en: activity, like solving crossword puzzles, and they were doing this activity on their own because they enjoy doing it.
sentences.zh: 活动（比如解填字游戏）的人面前，他们做这个活动完全是因为自己喜欢。

sentences.en: And he then offered to pay them a small amount of money for each time they finished a crossword puzzle.
sentences.zh: 然后他提出，每当他们完成一个填字游戏时，就支付给他们一小笔钱。

sentences.en: They, you know, paid them a dollar for every crossword puzzle they, they finish.
sentences.zh: 他们，你知道的，每完成一个填字游戏就付给他们一美元。

sentences.en: And of course you would think, well, this, this is going to increase their motivation to do crossword puzzles because they were doing them anyway.
sentences.zh: 当然你会认为，这，这会增加他们做填字游戏的动力，因为他们本来就在做。

sentences.en: And now they're getting paid for doing them.
sentences.zh: 而且现在他们做这个还能拿到报酬。

sentences.en: But what he found was over time, the volunteer stopped doing the crossword puzzles unless they received the dollar.
sentences.zh: 但他发现，随着时间的推移，除非拿到这一美元，否则志愿者们就不再做填字游戏了。

sentences.en: So in other words, the extrinsic motivation started to crowd out the intrinsic motivation, which is exactly what you are describing in the story with Marco
sentences.zh: 换句话说，外在动机开始排挤内在动机，这正是你在马尔科

sentences.en: Pierre White.
sentences.zh: ·皮埃尔·怀特的故事中所描述的那样。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，确实如此。

sentences.en: And there's other examples, even, even studies with children, you know, you have to, you ask them to make drawings and then, and, and this is what most children naturally
sentences.zh: 还有其他例子，甚至是对儿童的研究，你知道的，你让他们画画，然后，这正是大多数孩子天生

sentences.en: love to do.
sentences.zh: 喜欢做的事。

sentences.en: And then you start to pay them or give them some other kind of reward.
sentences.zh: 接着你开始付钱给他们，或者给他们其他形式的奖励。

sentences.en: And they actually start to, to like it less.
sentences.zh: 结果他们反而开始变得不那么喜欢它了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The big problem with extrinsic motivation is not the extrinsic motivation itself, but it's the eroding, as you said, of the intrinsic motivation.
sentences.zh: 外在动机最大的问题不在于外在动机本身，而在于它正如你所说，对内在动机的侵蚀。

sentences.en: You know, it's like a cuckoo in the nest, you know, it pushes the other eggs out.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就好比巢里的杜鹃，它会把别的鸟蛋挤出去。

sentences.en: I understand that you yourself had an experience in Ecuador some years ago that generated a moment of inspiration for you.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，几年前你本人在厄瓜多尔也有过一次经历，为你带来了灵感。

sentences.en: Tell me what happened up.
sentences.zh: 能跟我讲讲发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: I wanted to write a book about creativity.
sentences.zh: 我当时想写一本关于创造力的书。

sentences.en: And after about a year, I gave up because I liked the topic, but I didn't, I didn't have a good idea of what the book would be.
sentences.zh: 大约一年后我放弃了，因为我很喜欢这个主题，但我对这本书到底要写什么并没有一个清晰的想法。

sentences.en: It was all still very vague.
sentences.zh: 一切都还是非常模糊的。

sentences.en: And then about three, four years later, I tried again and again, I failed.
sentences.zh: 大约三、四年后，我又尝试了一次，结果还是失败了。

sentences.en: And then I was in, in Ecuador, in Quito, the capital, and there are four or five very old churches and suddenly dawned on me how amazing that was.
sentences.zh: 后来我在厄瓜多尔的首都基多，那里有四五座非常古老的教堂，我突然意识到这是多么令人惊叹。

sentences.en: You imagine it's 16th century, you're on a boat for many, many months, and then you land on the shore of Ecuador.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象那是16世纪，你在船上呆了许多许多个月，然后你在厄瓜多尔的海岸登陆。

sentences.en: And then with a group of people, you go into this crazy jungle and you walk for a couple of weeks until you reach a mountain range.
sentences.zh: 接着你和一群人走进这片疯狂的丛林，步行好几个星期，直到到达一处山脉。

sentences.en: And then you climb up to 8,000 feet.
sentences.zh: 然后你爬上海拔8000英尺的高山。

sentences.en: Your leader says, let's, let's make a couple churches here.
sentences.zh: 你的领队说，咱们，咱们在这里建几座教堂吧。

sentences.en: What these colonialists did, the first thing they did when they arrived there is build four or five of these huge churches that are obviously still standing there.
sentences.zh: 这些殖民者到达那里后做的第一件事，就是建造了四五座至今仍然耸立在那里的宏伟教堂。

sentences.en: They're beautiful.
sentences.zh: 它们美极了。

sentences.en: And then that's when it, when it dawned on me that the book shouldn't be about creativity, it should be about inspiration.
sentences.zh: 也就是在那时，我突然意识到这本书不该写创造力，而应该写灵感。

sentences.en: So for me, it was a very important moment.
sentences.zh: 所以对当时的我和我而言，这是一个非常重要的时刻。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You're clearly a fan of the Beatles because the Beatles have come up several times in our, our conversation.
sentences.zh: 你显然是披头士的粉丝，因为在我们的交谈中，披头士乐队已经被提及好几次了。

sentences.en: And you say that John Lennon and Paul McCartney had an unusual way of selecting the songs that they felt were worth keeping.
sentences.zh: 你说约翰·列侬和保罗·麦卡特尼有一种不同寻常的方法来挑选他们觉得值得保留的歌曲。

sentences.en: They generated, of course, many melodies and lyrics, but didn't always, you know, finish all of them or publish all of them.
sentences.zh: 他们当然创作了许多旋律和歌词，但你知道的，并非总是把它们全部完成或全部发表。

sentences.en: What was their process up?
sentences.zh: 他们的流程是怎样的？

sentences.en: They would jam in their studio and just come up with new songs all the time, but they didn't have any recording equipment at the time.
sentences.zh: 他们会在录音室里即兴创作，源源不断地想出新歌，但当时他们没有任何录音设备。

sentences.en: So they basically had to memorize what they did.
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上只能靠记忆记住他们创作的内容。

sentences.en: And then at some point, they just realized that, okay, if we play something in the afternoon, maybe we remember it the next morning and then it's probably good.
sentences.zh: 后来在某个时候，他们突然意识到，好吧，如果我们下午弹奏一段旋律，第二天早上还能想起来，那它可能就是首好歌。

sentences.en: And if we don't remember it the next morning, well, fine, because it's probably not good enough anyway.
sentences.zh: 如果我们第二天早上想不起来了，那也没关系，反正它可能也够不上好歌的标准。

sentences.en: So they had a very natural selection process in coming up with their songs.
sentences.zh: 因此，在创作歌曲时，他们采用了一种非常自然的筛选过程。

sentences.en: You know, it's striking to me, Op, as we are talking today, I'm realizing that in so many different ways,
sentences.zh: 你知道，令我感触很深的是，奥普，在我们今天的谈话中，我意识到在这么多不同的方面，

sentences.en: we are not in our daily lives, in our modern lives, really allowing the unconscious to flourish.
sentences.zh: 在我们的日常生活中，在现代生活中，我们并没有真正让无意识蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: You know, we write down every single thought we have.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们把产生的每一个想法都记下来。

sentences.en: We are so focused on our emails and our work.
sentences.zh: 我们把太多的精力放在电子邮件和工作上。

sentences.en: We're basically very directed in what we are trying to finish.
sentences.zh: 我们在试图完成什么事情时，目标性往往极强。

sentences.en: We have goals and we say, okay,
sentences.zh: 我们设立目标，然后说，好吧，

sentences.en: I'm going to work on this goal very closely.
sentences.zh: 我要紧盯着这个目标去努力。

sentences.en: And taking a day off every week to go and garden would be a waste of time.
sentences.zh: 而如果每周抽一天假去园艺，会被认为是在浪费时间。

sentences.en: Talk about the ways in which our modern world, in some ways, is working against the capacities of our unconscious minds to help us be creative?
sentences.zh: 谈谈我们的现代社会在哪些方面在某种程度上阻碍了我们无意识思维发挥创造力的潜能？

sentences.en: I think that basically all this modern technology, it's highly useful in some ways, but it also clutters our mind.
sentences.zh: 我认为基本上所有这些现代技术在某些方面非常有用，但它们也让我们的思维变得杂乱。

sentences.en: You know, these days you need to remember a password when you want to order something from your local butcher.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如今当你从当地的肉铺买东西时，你都得记住一个密码。

sentences.en: You know, it's pretty crazy these days.
sentences.zh: 你知道，现在这确实挺疯狂的。

sentences.en: And you have to almost literally clean your mind.
sentences.zh: 你几乎不得不字面意义上清空自己的大脑。

sentences.en: And you do this by, yeah, by things such as walking, by doing other things.
sentences.zh: 你通过，是的，通过散步、做其他事情来实现这一点。

sentences.en: And this frees up your unconscious mind again for things that you actually want to achieve for useful things.
sentences.zh: 这让你的无意识大脑再次腾出空间，去实现你真正想要达成的目标，去做那些有用的事情。

sentences.en: Email, let's face it, email these days is a to-do list where other people put things on.
sentences.zh: 面对现实吧，现在的电子邮件就是别人给你布置任务的待办清单。

sentences.en: And if you see it in this way, it's easier to sometimes just say, sorry, now I'm going to choose for myself.
sentences.zh: 如果你这样看待它，有时就会更容易说：对不起，现在我要为自己做选择。

sentences.en: Inspiration often feels like a bolt of lightning.
sentences.zh: 灵感通常感觉就像一道闪电。

sentences.en: As we've seen, there are a number of things we can do to make our minds hospitable places for creativity.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所见，我们可以做很多事情来让我们的头脑成为孕育创造力的沃土。
